The recital finds that the public interest requires that the employee be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year, and the operative sentence, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), exempts Hubert K. Bishop from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending June 30 of a year the held text prints as 1041 (read as 1941). That exemption is the order's only command and it carries its own fixed term. First end: the order's own stated end, June 30 of the year printed 1041 and read as 1941 (operative sentence: "for a period of one year ending June 30, 1041."). The stated date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of June 30, 1941); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when June 30, 1941 begins, is the alternative. The held text prints the end year as 1041, an evident misprint (the order is dated May 18, 1940, so an exemption ending in 1041 is impossible); the one-year period, the recital that the employee reaches retirement age in June 1940, and EO 8810 (below) support June 30, 1941. Like this order it has no effective-date wording, so I read it as effective on signing. The date recorded is June 30, 1941; EO 8810 recites a one-year exemption by this order and further exempts the employee for a year ending June 30, 1942, which fits an end of June 30, 1941.

source.page_or_item: Executive Order 8421—Exemption of Joseph E. Reardon From Compulsory Retirement for Age; May 28, 1940; APP node 371576; common-crawl capture 2024-12-13T15:40:51Z
source.quote:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Joseph F. Reardon, master joiner and shipwright, Navy Yard, New York, New York, who, during the current month, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to him, be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby exempt the said Joseph F. Reardon from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending May 31, 1941.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

The White House,

May 28, 1940.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 0-669 of the held text jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-8422-exemption-james-e-harper-from-compulsory-retirement-for-age.txt): signed May 28, 1940. The recital finds that the public interest requires that the employee be further exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year, and the operative sentence, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), further exempts James E. Harper from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending June 30, 1941. That exemption is the order's only command and it carries its own fixed term. The recital names the earlier exemption Executive Order No. 8139 of May 19, 1939; those are earlier instruments, not events on this order. First end: the order's own stated end, June 30, 1941 (operative sentence: "for a period of one year ending June 30, 1941."). The stated date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of June 30, 1941); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when June 30, 1941 begins, is the alternative. The date is the end of the stated term, not a record of separation or death; no such record is held. Later event, not an end: Executive Order 8804, signed June 25, 1941, further exempts the same person; its recital names this order ("Executive Orders No. 8139 of May 19, 1939, and No. 8422 of May 28, 1940") and its operative sentence runs "for a period of three months ending September 30, 1941". Like this order it has no effective-date wording, so I read it as effective on signing.

source.page_or_item: Executive Order 8804—Exemption of James E. Harper From Compulsory Retirement for Age; June 25, 1941; APP node 210614; common-crawl capture 2025-10-13T10:08:50Z
source.quote:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that James E. Harper, Chief, Employee Relations Section, Division of Personnel, Treasury Department, who was exempted from compulsory retirement for age for periods totaling two years by Executive Orders No. 8139 of May 19, 1939, and No. 8422 of May 28, 1940, be further exempted from such compulsory retirement for a period of three months:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby further exempt the said James E. Harper from compulsory retirement for age for a period of three months ending September 30, 1941.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

The White House,

June 25, 1941.

By virtue of and pursuant to the au­
thority vested in the President by sec­
tion 5 of Reorganization Plan No. T V , 
transmitted to the Congress on April 11, 
1940, I hereby prescribe the following 
rules and regulations governing the ad­
ministration by the Postmaster General 
of the Interbuilding Mail and Messenger 
Service transferred to and consolidated 
in the Post Office Department by the said 
section 5 of Reorganization Plan No. TV:
Sec. 1. There is hereby established in 
the Post Office Department a regularly 
scheduled pick-up and delivery service 
for the transmission of mail (including 
regular mail between Government agen­
cies and the City Post Office), papers, 
documents, packages, and other articles 
to and from buildings occupied by Gov­
ernment agencies within the District of 
Columbia and within that portion of the 
State of Virginia lying within a radius of 
3.5 miles from the southwest end of the 
Arlington Memorial Bridge. This serv­
ice shall be known as the United States 
Official Mail and Messenger Service and 
shall be under the direction and super­
vision of the Postmaster General.
Sec. 2. Vehicles used in this service 
shall bear the inscription "U. S. OFFI­
CIAL MAIL AND MESSENGER SERV­
ICE.” No other Government agency 
shall use or display such inscription or 
words of similar meaning on vehicles.
Sec. 3. The Postmaster General, or 
such official as he may designate, shall, 
from time to time, prescribe and pub­
lish for the information of all con­
cerned suitable schedules for the per­
formance of this service with a fre­
quency of not more than one trip per 
hour to each point of contact, except 
that such additional trips as may be 
deemed necessary may be scheduled for 
the collection and delivery of regular
mail between Government agencies and 
the City Post Office.
Sec. 4. Unless otherwise directed, the 
messengers in this service shall call on 
their scheduled rounds at one desig­
nated point in each building or each 
group of contiguous buildings occupied 
by a Government agency. The head of 
each Government agency concerned 
shall establish contact with this service 
in each building or each group of con­
tiguous buildings under his supervision 
at a point easily and quickly accessible 
to a loading dock or street entrance.
Sec. 5. This service shall not be re­
quired to accept for transmission any 
article weighing more than 100 pounds 
or measuring more than 100 inches in 
length and girth combined, but it may 
in its discretion accept other articles if 
such acceptance is found practicable.
Sec. 6. The Postmaster General may 
prescribe such distinctive types of enve­
lopes, tags, and labels for use in the 
transmission of matter by this service as 
may be necessary for efficient operation. 
Each agency concerned shall provide 
such quantities of these envelopes, tags, 
and labels as may be necessary for its 
own needs.
Sec. 7. The Postmaster General may 
prescribe such regulations not incon­
sistent herewith as may be necessary for 
carrying out the provisions of this order.
Sec. 8. This order shall become effec­
tive upon the effective date of the said 
Reorganization Plan No. T V .

It revokes section 2 of Executive Order No. 6228 of July 28, 1933, which interpreted the order of June 10, 1933, only insofar as that section pertains to or affects the transfer of the Custer Battlefield National Cemetery in Montana, and provides that the order becomes effective on "July 1,1940". Its one command is a revocation, performed when it took effect; it imposes no continuing duty and has no term. First end: performance on the stated effective date, 1940-07-01. This is the order's own stated date; the exact moment of effect within that day is not stated. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-28 (evidence not convenience) the exhausted command is separated from its surviving consequence (see savings). No earlier end: before July 1, 1940 the order had not taken effect, and no held text suspends, postpones or revokes it.

By virtue of and pursuant to the au­
thority vested in the President by sec­
tion 5 of Reorganization Plan No. T V , 
transmitted to the Congress on April 11, 
1940, I hereby prescribe the following 
rules and regulations governing the ad­
ministration by the Postmaster General 
of the Interbuilding Mail and Messenger 
Service transferred to and consolidated 
in the Post Office Department by the said 
section 5 of Reorganization Plan No. TV:
Sec. 1. There is hereby established in 
the Post Office Department a regularly 
scheduled pick-up and delivery service 
for the transmission of mail (including 
regular mail between Government agen­
cies and the City Post Office), papers, 
documents, packages, and other articles 
to and from buildings occupied by Gov­
ernment agencies within the District of 
Columbia and within that portion of the 
State of Virginia lying within a radius of 
3.5 miles from the southwest end of the 
Arlington Memorial Bridge. This serv­
ice shall be known as the United States 
Official Mail and Messenger Service and 
shall be under the direction and super­
vision of the Postmaster General.
Sec. 2. Vehicles used in this service 
shall bear the inscription "U. S. OFFI­
CIAL MAIL AND MESSENGER SERV­
ICE.” No other Government agency 
shall use or display such inscription or 
words of similar meaning on vehicles.
Sec. 3. The Postmaster General, or 
such official as he may designate, shall, 
from time to time, prescribe and pub­
lish for the information of all con­
cerned suitable schedules for the per­
formance of this service with a fre­
quency of not more than one trip per 
hour to each point of contact, except 
that such additional trips as may be 
deemed necessary may be scheduled for 
the collection and delivery of regular
mail between Government agencies and 
the City Post Office.
Sec. 4. Unless otherwise directed, the 
messengers in this service shall call on 
their scheduled rounds at one desig­
nated point in each building or each 
group of contiguous buildings occupied 
by a Government agency. The head of 
each Government agency concerned 
shall establish contact with this service 
in each building or each group of con­
tiguous buildings under his supervision 
at a point easily and quickly accessible 
to a loading dock or street entrance.
Sec. 5. This service shall not be re­
quired to accept for transmission any 
article weighing more than 100 pounds 
or measuring more than 100 inches in 
length and girth combined, but it may 
in its discretion accept other articles if 
such acceptance is found practicable.
Sec. 6. The Postmaster General may 
prescribe such distinctive types of enve­
lopes, tags, and labels for use in the 
transmission of matter by this service as 
may be necessary for efficient operation. 
Each agency concerned shall provide 
such quantities of these envelopes, tags, 
and labels as may be necessary for its 
own needs.
Sec. 7. The Postmaster General may 
prescribe such regulations not incon­
sistent herewith as may be necessary for 
carrying out the provisions of this order.
Sec. 8. This order shall become effec­
tive upon the effective date of the said 
Reorganization Plan No. T V .

cies and the City Post Office), papers, 
documents, packages, and other articles 
to and from buildings occupied by Gov­
ernment agencies within the District of 
Columbia and within that portion of the 
State of Virginia lying within a radius of 
3.5 miles from the southwest end of the 
Arlington Memorial Bridge. This serv­
ice shall be known as the United States 
Official Mail and Messenger Service and 
shall be under the direction and super­
vision of the Postmaster General.
Sec. 2. Vehicles used in this service 
shall bear the inscription "U. S. OFFI­
CIAL MAIL AND MESSENGER SERV­
ICE.” No other Government agency 
shall use or display such inscription or 
words of similar meaning on vehicles.
Sec. 3. The Postmaster General, or 
such official as he may designate, shall, 
from time to time, prescribe and pub­
lish for the information of all con­
cerned suitable schedules for the per­
formance of this service with a fre­
quency of not more than one trip per 
hour to each point of contact, except 
that such additional trips as may be 
deemed necessary may be scheduled for 
the collection and delivery of regular
mail between Government agencies and 
the City Post Office.
Sec. 4. Unless otherwise directed, the 
messengers in this service shall call on 
their scheduled rounds at one desig­
nated point in each building or each 
group of contiguous buildings occupied 
by a Government agency. The head of 
each Government agency concerned 
shall establish contact with this service 
in each building or each group of con­
tiguous buildings under his supervision 
at a point easily and quickly accessible 
to a loading dock or street entrance.
Sec. 5. This service shall not be re­
quired to accept for transmission any 
article weighing more than 100 pounds 
or measuring more than 100 inches in 
length and girth combined, but it may 
in its discretion accept other articles if 
such acceptance is found practicable.
Sec. 6. The Postmaster General may 
prescribe such distinctive types of enve­
lopes, tags, and labels for use in the 
transmission of matter by this service as 
may be necessary for efficient operation. 
Each agency concerned shall provide 
such quantities of these envelopes, tags, 
and labels as may be necessary for its 
own needs.
Sec. 7. The Postmaster General may 
prescribe such regulations not incon­
sistent herewith as may be necessary for 
carrying out the provisions of this order.
Sec. 8. This order shall become effec­
tive upon the effective date of the said 
Reorganization Plan No. T V .

operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Maitland S. Wright, Chief, Supply Unit, Department of State, who, during the month of July, 1940, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to him, be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby exempt the said Maitland S. Wright from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending July 31, 1941.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

The recital finds that the public interest requires that the employee be further exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year, and the operative sentence, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), further exempts Harry T. Edwards from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending October 31, 1941. That exemption is the order's only command and it carries its own fixed term. The recital names the earlier exemption Executive Order No. 8259 of September 21, 1939; those are earlier instruments, not events on this order. First end: the order's own stated end, October 31, 1941 (operative sentence: "for a period of one year ending October 31, 1941."). The stated date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of October 31, 1941); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when October 31, 1941 begins, is the alternative. The date is the end of the stated term, not a record of separation or death; no such record is held. Later event, not an end: Executive Order 8827, signed July 24, 1941, further exempts the same person; its recital names this order ("Executive Orders No. 8259 of September 21, 1939, and No. 8525 of August 26, 1940") and its operative sentence runs "ending October 31, 1941". Like this order it has no effective-date wording, so I read it as effective on signing. The period that EO 8827 states ends on the same day as the period of this order; a later order, EO 8844 of August 8, 1941, amends EO 8827 (not this order) so that its period ends October 31, 1942. EO 8844 does not name this order and is not an event on it; I read it because the name search listed it.

source.quote:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Harry T. Edwards, senior technologist, Bureau of Plant Industry, Department of Agriculture, who was exempted from compulsory retirement for age for periods totaling two years by Executive Orders No. 8259 of September 21, 1939, and No. 8525 of August 26, 1940, be further exempted from such compulsory retirement for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby further exempt the said Harry T. Edwards from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending October 31, 1941.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

The White House,

July 24, 1941.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 3082-3391 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_8529.txt; 5 FR 3403, issue of Friday, August 30, 1940): signed August 27, 1940 under the act of June 25, 1910 (36 Stat. 847). It revokes Executive Order No. 4901 of June 4, 1928, which withdrew public land for classification and in aid of legislation in New Mexico, and says it becomes effective on "the sixtieth day from the date hereof." Its one command is a revocation, performed when it took effect; it has no term and no continuing duty. First end: performance on the effective date. The date is computed, not stated: the sixtieth day after August 27, 1940, excluding the signing day, is October 26, 1940 (4 days to August 31, 30 to September 30, 26 to October 26). If the signing day were counted as day 1 the date would be October 25, 1940; I record October 26 and disclose the alternative. No earlier end: the order had no effect before its effective date and no held text suspends or revokes it.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Whole order (single paragraph, offsets 4545-6049 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_8536.txt; 5 FR 3606, issue of Tuesday, September 10, 1940): signed September 6, 1940. It amends Executive Order No. 7747 of November 20, 1937 (a defensive sea area off San Clemente Island, California) by substituting one nautical mile for three hundred yards in its first paragraph and adding the area's name, and then reproduces EO 7747 as thus amended: the water surrounding the island out to one nautical mile beyond low-water mark is a defensive sea area, subject to the Commerce Department uses reserved by EO 6897; no vessel or craft may be navigated in it except as the Secretary of the Navy authorizes; and violators are subject to the penalties provided by law. The amendment instruction was performed on signing, but the reproduced text (area, vessel restriction, penalty) is the order's continuing content and has no term of its own. Later event, not an end: Executive Order 9787, signed October 5, 1946 (11 FR 11556), amends EO 7747 as amended by EO 8536 "to read as follows" and restates the whole text. Before: area out to one nautical mile beyond low-water mark. After: three hundred yards beyond low-water mark, except one hundred yards in Wilson Cove, and including the part of Pyramid Cove north of a described line; the vessel restriction and penalty paragraphs are carried over in the same terms. This rewrite replaces the whole section and changes the substance of the area. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (strike and insert) the clause continues, amended, and the amendment is recorded as a later event. A reviewer who reads EO 9787 as superseding this order's text would date the end at 1946-10-05 instead. First end: Executive Order 9894, signed September 23, 1947 (12 FR 6353, issue of September 25, 1947; filed September 23, 1947), which orders under section 44 of the Criminal Code (18 U.S.C. 96) that the San Clemente Island Naval Defensive Sea Area, established by EO 7747 as amended by EO 8536 and EO 9787, be discontinued. It names this order by number and discontinues the area that its text establishes. It has no effective-date wording, so I read it as effective on signing, 1947-09-23; the filing and printing dates are not effective dates.

EXECUTIVE ORDER
E stablishing  S an C lemente  I sland N aval 
D efensive  S ea A rea
CALIFORNIA
Executive Order No. 7747, dated No­
vember 20,1937,1  establishing a defensive  
sea area off the coast of San Clemente  
Island, California, is hereby amended by  
substituting the words “one nautical  
mile” for the words “three hundred  
yards” as they appear in the first para­
graph thereof, and by adding at the end  
of said first paragraph the following  
words: “Said defensive sea area shall  
be known as San Clemente Island Naval  
Defensive Sea Area”. As thus amended  
said Executive order reads as follows:  
“By virtue of and pursuant to the  
authority vested in me by the provisions 
of section 44 of the Criminal Code, as  
amended (U.S.C., title 18, sec. 96), the
area of water surrounding San Clemente  
Island, California, extending from low  
water mark out for a distance of one  
nautical mile beyond low-water mark, is  
hereby established as a defensive sea area  
for purposes of national defense, subject  
to the uses reserved for the Department  
of Commerce in Executive Order No  
6897, dated November 7, 1934. Said de­
fensive sea area shall be known as San  
Clemente Island Naval Defensive Sea  Area.
“At no time shall vessels or other craft  
be navigated within the defensive sea  
area above defined except such as are  
authorized by the Secretary of the Navy.
“Any person violating the provisions of  
this order shall be subject to the pen­
alties provided by law.”

operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Herbert A. Howell, Assistant Register of Copyrights, The Library of Congress, who, during the current month, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to him, be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby exempt the said Herbert A. Howell from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1941.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 0-686 of the held text jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-8555-exemption-samuel-cottrell-from-compulsory-retirement-for-age.txt): signed September 28, 1940. The recital finds that the public interest requires that the employee be further exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of nine months, and the operative sentence, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), further exempts Samuel A. Cottrell from compulsory retirement for age for a period of nine months ending June 30, 1941. That exemption is the order's only command and it carries its own fixed term. The recital names the earlier exemption Executive Order No. 8262 of September 26, 1939; those are earlier instruments, not events on this order. First end: the order's own stated end, June 30, 1941 (operative sentence: "for a period of nine months ending June 30, 1941."). The stated date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of June 30, 1941); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when June 30, 1941 begins, is the alternative. The date is the end of the stated term, not a record of separation or death; no such record is held. Later event, not an end: Executive Order 8805, signed June 25, 1941, further exempts the same person; its recital names this order ("Executive Orders No. 8262 of September 26, 1939, and No. 8555 of September 28, 1940") and its operative sentence runs "ending June 30, 1942". Like this order it has no effective-date wording, so I read it as effective on signing.

source.page_or_item: Executive Order 8805—Exemption of Samuel A. Cottrell From Compulsory Retirement for Age; June 25, 1941; APP node 368276; common-crawl capture 2025-10-09T14:28:41Z
source.quote:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Samuel A. Cottrell, auditor, Income Tax Unit, Bureau of Internal Revenue, Treasury Department, who was exempted from compulsory retirement for age for periods totaling one year and nine months by Executive Orders No. 8262 of September 26, 1939, and No. 8555 of September 28, 1940, be further exempted from such compulsory retirement for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby further exempt the said Samuel A. Cottrell from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending June 30, 1942.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

The White House,

June 25, 1941.

The recital finds that the public interest requires that the employee be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year, and the operative sentence, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), exempts James C. Wynde from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending November 30, 1941. That exemption is the order's only command and it carries its own fixed term. First end: the order's own stated end, November 30, 1941 (operative sentence: "for a period of one year ending November 30, 1941."). The stated date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of November 30, 1941); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when November 30, 1941 begins, is the alternative. The date is the end of the stated term, not a record of separation or death; no such record is held.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that James C. Wynde, Deputy Collector of Customs, Treasury Department, who, during the current month, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to him, be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby exempt the said James C. Wynde from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending November 30, 1941.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT
